title: Drag-destination-only tools are forced through source-coordinate validation
reasoning: The facade always calls source-coordinate preparation before drag-destination preparation. The source helper does not first check whether the tool actually supports source grounding; non-OCR/PREDICTION calls fall into the manual branch and require top-level x/y. A tool that only needs drag destination grounding, or a drag call whose source is already executable but whose destination needs resolution, can fail with 'Manual coordinates require numeric x and y values' before the destination helper gets a chance to resolve drag_to_* coordinates. The separate supports_drag_destination_grounding gate in the destination helper indicates destination grounding is an independent capability, but the call order makes it dependent on source-coordinate validity.
recommendation: Gate resolve_grounded_source_coordinates behind supports_source_grounding or tool_call_has_manual/source-resolution need, then run drag-destination resolution independently when supports_drag_destination_grounding applies.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included coordinate-resolution tests cover OCR/PREDICTION source paths only and do not exercise resolve_tool_with_coordinates with a drag-destination grounding case that lacks valid top-level x/y.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend test for resolve_tool_with_coordinates where a drag action has drag_to_find_coordinates_by requiring OCR/PREDICTION and no top-level x/y; assert destination coordinates are resolved without the source helper raising.
minimumFixScope: preparation_helper.py and/or grounded_source_preparation.py, plus a focused backend regression test.
